vote: The use nailed the skeleton — JOB/IN/OUT contract written before prose, 'Use when PR request / Conductor attachment' plus a 'Skip when commit-or-push-only' fence, six steps each ending on a Done-when, evals and logging sections shipped, and the usage line itself is a model log entry (bounded excerpt, local -0400 offset) — but it fails the artifact's own Done-when checklist and still logs 'success': install.sh was deliberately skipped (worktree symlinks would point at the wrong root), which per the checklist makes this a partial at best, and 'false pass' is exactly the catastrophic failure class section 4 tells authors to guard against. Three lacks in the artifact this exposes: (1) the Done-when demands './install.sh run' unconditionally with no branch for authoring from a Conductor worktree — add an explicit deferred-install path (log outcome 'partial' with a named follow-up, or a post-merge install step) instead of forcing authors to improvise in notes; (2) the excerpt evidences none of the least-checkable requirements — section 0 dedupe, the leading word (the checklist's own 'Use when + leading word + Skip when' triad shows only two of three here), or eval-content quality (>=5 cases, holdout marking, rubric catastrophics) — the logging spec should require one-token evidence for these or they will be silently skipped every run; (3) 'Grow cases from real usage-log failures and judge votes, not imagination' is structurally unsatisfiable for a brand-new skill with zero usage — the artifact needs a bootstrap rule for first-authoring cases. Repeated-failure hint: checklist items that cost effort at the end of a run (install, dedupe evidence, holdout hygiene) get waived in notes while outcome stays 'success', so define outcome semantics explicitly: success means every Done-when item met, nothing less.
